title: Pilot install runbook (draft) — Redwood Private air‑gapped + signed offline bundles
linked_artifacts: GitHub: redwood-private-installer PR-24888 (offline bundle inspect command)
GitHub: redwood-private-installer PR-24979 (break-glass flag + audit warning)
Jira: SUP-31844 (air-gapped install fails signature verification)
body:
Context / who this is for
- This is a working runbook for pilot customer installs of Redwood Private in air-gapped/offline environments.
- Audience: Solutions/PS running the install (Bruno/Colin), Support (Dev/Owen), and Eng on-call (Ethan/SRE).
- Assumes signed offline bundles are enabled for this pilot cohort.

Pilot goals (what “done” means)
- Customer can verify the bundle signature offline before install.
- Installer preflight blocks on tampering/untrusted key/mismatch and provides actionable output.
- Install completes without needing outbound network access.
- If verification fails, we collect the right artifacts on first pass (reduce back-and-forth).

Non-goals / guardrails
- Do not use break-glass except with explicit approval (see Break-glass section). It creates audit markers and increases supply-chain risk.
- Do not “work around” verification errors by editing the manifest or swapping files; this invalidates evidence and makes the problem harder to debug.

Terminology
- Offline bundle: customer-transferred bundle (e.g., .tar.gz) containing manifests, charts, image references, runtime/model artifacts, etc.
- Manifest: canonical manifest file (e.g., bundle.manifest.json) listing hashes/versions.
- Signature: detached signature file (e.g., bundle.manifest.sig) for the manifest.
- Trust store: installer’s trusted public keys / cert chain (may be embedded or provided via file, depending on pilot setup).

Pre-req checklist (do this before scheduling the install)
1) Confirm pilot package versions
- Installer version: ______________
- Bundle version: ______________
- Bundle build ID (if present): ______________
- Kubernetes version + distro: ______________
- Container runtime (containerd/docker) + version: ______________

2) Confirm environment constraints
- Truly air-gapped (no outbound) vs restricted outbound.
- Time source: NTP allowed? manual clock set? known time skew risk?
- Allowed crypto requirements (some customers restrict algorithms / FIPS).

3) Confirm access + tooling on the jump host
- We need a jump host (or admin workstation) that can run:
  - redwood-private-installer (Linux x86_64 typically)
  - tar, sha256sum, openssl (optional, helpful)
  - kubectl + access to target cluster
- Disk space: bundle can be large (plan for 2x bundle size for extraction).

4) Confirm transport plan for the offline bundle
- Prefer: transfer the exact tarball as received (avoid re-zipping).
- Avoid Windows “Extract All” or tools that may alter filenames/permissions.
- Record chain-of-custody:
  - who downloaded
  - checksum at download site
  - checksum after transfer

5) Confirm we have the customer’s expected trust root update method
- If customer needs to import Redwood signing public keys into their local trust store file, confirm how they want that delivered (USB, internal artifact repo, etc.).


Artifacts we will ask the customer to provide (set expectations upfront)
If anything fails, we’ll request:
- The original bundle tarball (or at minimum the manifest + signature files) AND the checksum they computed post-transfer.
- Installer logs + preflight output.
- The installer support bundle (if enabled).
- System time + timezone info from the jump host.


Install flow (high level)
A) Validate the bundle was transferred intact (hashes)
B) Verify bundle signature (offline)
C) Run installer preflight (must verify signature + manifest)
D) Install
E) Post-install verification (cluster health + version correlation)


A) Validate transfer integrity (before extraction)
1) Compute checksum of the received tarball
- On jump host:
  - sha256sum <bundle-file>.tar.gz | tee bundle.sha256
- Compare with the checksum provided by Redwood Release Eng (or the secure download portal).
- If mismatch: stop here. Don’t extract.

2) Record basic metadata
- Filename:
- Size (ls -lh):
- sha256:
- Date/time computed:

Notes:
- We have seen corruption due to:
  - partial transfers
  - “smart” unzip tools rewriting files
  - newline conversion on manifest files when copied incorrectly


B) Verify signature (offline) BEFORE running install
Preferred approach: use installer built-in inspection/verify (keeps output consistent for Support).

1) Extract bundle (if required by tool)
- mkdir -p /var/tmp/redwood-bundle && cd /var/tmp/redwood-bundle
- tar -xzf /path/to/<bundle>.tar.gz

2) Inspect bundle layout
- Expected key files (names may vary by pilot build; confirm in release notes):
  - bundle.manifest.json
  - bundle.manifest.sig (detached signature)
  - sbom/… (optional)
  - charts/… (helm chart tarballs)
  - images/… (image list + digests; images may be separately transported)
  - artifacts/… (runtime/model artifacts)

3) Run bundle inspection + signature verify
- Command (pilot default):
  - redwood-private-installer offline-bundle inspect --bundle /var/tmp/redwood-bundle --verify-signature
- Capture output (copy/paste into notes and save to file):
  - redwood-private-installer offline-bundle inspect --bundle /var/tmp/redwood-bundle --verify-signature | tee inspect.txt

Expected output characteristics (not exact text)
- “Signature: VALID”
- “Signing key: <key-id>”
- “Manifest canonicalization: OK”
- “Manifest schema version: <v>”
- “Bundle version: <x.y.z> (build <id>)”

If output indicates invalid/untrusted signature: do NOT proceed. Go to Failure Handling.

Time skew warning
- Some signature envelopes include validity windows.
- If the jump host clock is wrong (common in air-gapped), verification may fail as “not yet valid” / “expired”.
- Collect time info immediately:
  - date -u
  - timedatectl (if systemd)


C) Run installer preflight (must fail closed)
1) Preflight command
- Example:
  - redwood-private-installer preflight --air-gapped --bundle /var/tmp/redwood-bundle --output preflight.json
- Also capture human-readable output:
  - redwood-private-installer preflight --air-gapped --bundle /var/tmp/redwood-bundle 2>&1 | tee preflight.txt

2) What preflight should check (minimum)
- Signature verification + trusted key check
- Manifest hash validation (every listed artifact hash matches)
- Downgrade prevention (if prior install state exists)
- Kubernetes connectivity + RBAC
- Disk space
- No outbound fetch attempts in air-gapped mode

3) If preflight passes
- Proceed to install.


D) Install
1) Install command (example; adjust to customer’s environment)
- redwood-private-installer install --air-gapped --bundle /var/tmp/redwood-bundle --namespace redwood-private

2) During install, record
- Start time / end time
- Any warnings (copy into notes)
- Cluster events if there are delays:
  - kubectl get events -n redwood-private --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50

3) If install fails
- Stop and collect artifacts (see Failure Handling) before retrying repeatedly.


E) Post-install verification
1) Confirm deployed versions
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-private
- kubectl describe deploy/<key components> -n redwood-private | egrep -i "image:|app.kubernetes.io/version|build"

2) Correlate running cluster to bundle build ID (if annotations/labels enabled)
- kubectl get deploy -n redwood-private -o jsonpath='{..metadata.annotations}' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -i bundle

3) Confirm audit events (local)
- If audit logging is configured locally, confirm we see:
  - bundle_verification_success (or equivalent)
  - install_started / install_completed
- If the customer forwards to SIEM, confirm mapping is enabled per pilot plan.


Failure handling (signature/manifest verification failures)

Golden rule
- Do not attempt installation when verification fails, unless break-glass is approved.

Common failure modes + what to do

1) Hash mismatch (manifest lists sha256 that doesn’t match local file)
Symptoms
- Installer says “hash mismatch” for a specific path, or “manifest mismatch / artifact digest mismatch”.
Likely causes
- Corrupt transfer
- Extract tool modified permissions/line endings (rare but seen)
- Bundle contents changed (tampering or accidental)
Immediate actions
- Identify the file path reported and compute sha256 locally:
  - sha256sum <reported-file>
- Compute sha256 of the original tarball too.
- Ask customer to re-transfer using different tool/media if tarball hash mismatch.
Collect
- preflight.txt + preflight.json
- inspect.txt
- sha256 of tarball + sha256 of the mismatched file
- exact unzip/tar tool + version used

2) Unknown signing key / untrusted root
Symptoms
- “unknown key id” or “signing key not in trust store”.
Likely causes
- Customer is using an older installer trust store (post-rotation mismatch)
- Trust store file not updated/loaded
Immediate actions
- Confirm installer version and trust store configuration.
- Ask for “signing key id” displayed by inspect output.
- If trust store update is required, coordinate with Release Eng + Security before distributing keys.
Collect
- inspect.txt (must include key id)
- installer version output:
  - redwood-private-installer version
- trust store path + contents (redact if needed; at least list key IDs)

3) Signature invalid
Symptoms
- “signature invalid” / “failed to verify signature”.
Likely causes
- Manifest changed (tampering or accidental edit)
- Wrong signature file paired with manifest (mixing builds)
Immediate actions
- Confirm manifest + signature are from same bundle build.
- Do not proceed.
Collect
- bundle.manifest.json + bundle.manifest.sig from the customer host (as-is)
- inspect.txt
- sha256 of both files

4) Not-yet-valid / expired (time skew)
Symptoms
- Verification fails with time validity errors.
Likely causes
- Jump host clock wrong (air-gapped with no NTP)
Immediate actions
- Capture system time and timezone.
- If customer policy allows: correct time and retry verify.
- If customer cannot change time, we may need the diagnostics time override (if enabled in this pilot build). Do not use overrides without telling Support/Eng.
Collect
- date -u output
- timedatectl output
- inspect.txt + preflight.txt

5) Downgrade prevention triggered
Symptoms
- “downgrade not allowed” / “installed version is newer than bundle”.
Immediate actions
- Confirm intent (are we trying to rollback?).
- Follow approved rollback procedure (separate runbook); do not force install.
Collect
- installer state record location + contents (redact secrets)
- target bundle version and current installed version


What to collect (copy/paste checklist)
When any verification/preflight/install step fails, collect:
- [ ] Command run (exact)
- [ ] Full stdout/stderr output (preflight.txt / install.txt / inspect.txt)
- [ ] Installer version (redwood-private-installer version)
- [ ] Bundle metadata (bundle version, build ID, manifest schema version)
- [ ] SHA256 of bundle tarball on customer side
- [ ] SHA256 of bundle tarball on Redwood side (from release notes / portal)
- [ ] If hash mismatch: sha256 of the specific mismatched file
- [ ] System time info: date -u, timedatectl
- [ ] Installer log files path(s) and archived logs
- [ ] Support bundle artifact (if available)
- [ ] Kubernetes events from namespace (if install progressed)

Log locations (best-effort; verify per installer build)
- Installer logs:
  - /var/log/redwood-private-installer/installer.log
  - /var/log/redwood-private-installer/preflight.log
- Preflight JSON output:
  - location passed via --output
- Audit/telemetry (local):
  - /var/log/redwood-private-installer/audit.log (or configured audit sink)

If paths differ, run:
- redwood-private-installer diagnostics paths
(or search for “redwood-private-installer” under /var/log)


Escalation + comms plan (pilot)

Severity guide (pilot-specific)
- Sev 1: customer blocked from install for >4 business hours during scheduled window OR repeated signature verification failures across re-transfer.
- Sev 2: install can proceed but verification UX unclear / missing evidence / intermittent pipeline issues.
- Sev 3: doc gaps, minor warnings, requests for enhancements.

Who to page / contact
- Support readiness lead: Dev Patel (triage owner for pilot escalations)
- Support engineer (pilot queue): Owen Phillips
- Installer/verification Eng lead: Ethan Park
- Release engineering (signing pipeline, key issues): Connor O'Brien
- Security Eng (signing/trust concerns): Marcus Lin
- SRE (install reliability/runbooks): Sean Gallagher
- Telemetry/audit events: Logan Wright

Contact details (internal)
- Slack channels:
  - #support (for ticket + customer comms coordination)
  - #eng-private-deployments (installer + on-prem packaging)
  - #eng-releases (signing pipeline / build questions)
  - #eng-security (trust store, key compromise concerns)
- Jira:
  - If customer-facing: open/attach to SUP ticket
  - If internal fix needed: create ENG ticket and link SUP

What to post in the escalation thread (template)
- Customer + environment: <name>, k8s <version>, distro <>, air-gapped yes/no
- Installer version: <>
- Bundle version/build ID: <>
- Error summary: <>
- Repro steps (commands): <>
- Artifacts attached: inspect.txt, preflight.txt/json, sha256, time info, logs
- What we tried: <>
- Is break-glass being requested? yes/no


Break-glass (last resort)
- Break-glass is only for cases where:
  - customer install is mission-critical and blocked,
  - AND we have explicit written approval per exception process,
  - AND we capture the required audit evidence.
- If a customer asks for break-glass:
  1) Stop and open a SUP ticket if not already.
  2) Escalate to Dev Patel + Marcus Lin + Connor O'Brien.
  3) Require customer acknowledgment that verification is being bypassed (text in email or ticket).

Break-glass command (example; do not use unless approved)
- redwood-private-installer preflight --air-gapped --bundle /var/tmp/redwood-bundle --break-glass-allow-unsigned
- Expected behavior: installer prints warnings, emits explicit audit marker.

Evidence to capture if break-glass used
- Screenshot/text of approval in ticket/email
- Full terminal output showing warning banner
- Audit log excerpt showing break_glass_used event
- Follow-up plan: restore normal signed verification ASAP


Notes / open questions (keep this section “messy”)
- Confirm final bundle file naming convention for GA (currently varies between pilot builds).
- Decide whether we always require detached signature vs allow embedded envelope in later phase.
- Verify which pilots will receive external trust-store file vs embedded keys only.
- Add a one-pager for customers on “how to verify the tarball checksum after transfer” (we keep getting this question).
- Time skew handling: do we want a read-only diagnostics override for verify (prints what time it thinks it is) without bypassing validity checks?

Change log (informal)
- 2025-11-26: initial draft from Helios Defense pilot planning.
- 2026-01-08: added sections on key rotation / unknown key.
- 2026-02-14: expanded artifact collection + escalation template; aligned with installer inspect command output.
